The scale on this one is just a bit smaller than I was hoping for. Still a great piece, but feels maybe a bit small even with 28mm scale models.

The module nature of the elevated walkways means you can adjust the layout easily. The walkways supported by the pillars actually have holes that line up with holes along the tall and short platform sections. With a bit of work, you could set pegs (probably two pegs and the rest magnets to help hold the pieces together during play) into these and forego the support pillars entirely.

This set came with two extra short-wall pieces, which can be used to either replace one Ladder Wall section entirely, or to set a Ladder Wall section to the center of one of the sides.

Very happy with the quality of the print job and the scale it is printed at for use with 28/32mm scale war games.

If you or someone you love is a fan of the dexterity/action game KLASK, then you know how the tiny biscuits, balls and bats can disappear in the bottom of the box, or roll off the table. 

This 3-D printed box has spaces for all of the pieces in a standard two player game, and a lid that slides on very snug. Sometimes it is a bit too snug but given how the bits can roll anywhere maybe that isn't too bad. 

The price is a bit steep (about 50% of the actual game, but as a display case it is eye-catching, and if you take the game with you it can be invaluable as a replacement for a baggie.
It's practical, fits well with the theme of the game, and when stacked 2 on top of each other, they won't fall out in the box, even if you turn them upside down.
